stages.name: Observe
stages.instruction: A Torricelli barometer: an inverted tube of mercury standing in an open reservoir. The atmosphere pushes on the pool and holds a column of mercury of height $h$ in the tube. Sweep the three sliders — altitude $z$, sea-level pressure $p_0$, and air temperature $T$ — and watch how each one moves the column.
stages.concept: The column obeys $p_\text{atm} = \rho_\text{Hg}\,g\,h$ (Torricelli). The atmosphere thins with height as $p_\text{atm}(z) = p_0\,e^{-z/H}$, with scale height $H = R\,T/(M\,g) \approx 8.4$ km at $T \approx 288$ K. Higher altitude $\to$ lower $p_\text{atm}$ $\to$ shorter column.

stages.name: Experiment
stages.instruction: A target mercury height $h^*$ is marked on the tube. Adjust $z$, $p_0$ and $T$ until the live column meets the target line. Many triples will work: what matters is the resulting $p_\text{atm}$.
stages.concept: Rearranging: $h = \dfrac{p_0\,e^{-z/H(T)}}{\rho_\text{Hg}\,g}$. Since three parameters produce one column height, dozens of triples solve it. Pick one variable to move first (usually $z$), then trim with the others.

stages.name: Evaluate
stages.instruction: The mercury column is hidden. Only the target $h^*$ tick and the slider readouts remain. Compute a valid $(z, p_0, T)$ triple on paper first, set the sliders, then submit. A wrong submit rotates you to a new target — no brute-force retries.
stages.concept: Blind inverse: $p_\text{atm}^* = \rho_\text{Hg}\,g\,h^*$, then $e^{-z/H} = p_\text{atm}^* / p_0$, giving $z = H\,\ln(p_0 / p_\text{atm}^*)$. Convert units carefully: $1\text{ mmHg} = 133.322\text{ Pa}$, $1\text{ hPa} = 100\text{ Pa}$.

labels.tip1: sweep each slider across at least half its range
labels.tip2: align the mercury column top with the target tick
labels.tip3: compute on paper first: p* = ρHg g h*, then solve for z
labels.peek_tip_formula: peek: h* = p0 e^(-z/H) / (rho_Hg g). Solve for z: z = H ln(p0 / p*).
labels.peek_tip_anchor: peek: 1 mmHg = 133.3 Pa; 1 hPa = 100 Pa; 1 bar = 750 mmHg.

1.1: Move altitude z from 0 upward: the mercury column should shorten smoothly.
1.2: At fixed altitude, raise p0 — the column climbs. Same physics, different knob.
1.3: Temperature affects the scale height H = RT/(Mg): warmer air = taller H = slower fall of p with altitude.

2.1: Read the target tick — that is your h*. Pick one variable to move first (altitude is the strongest).
2.2: If the column is too tall: raise altitude, lower p0, or lower T. Too short: opposite.
2.3: Solve h = p0 e^(-z/H) / (rho_Hg g) for one variable. Fixing p0 = 101 kPa and T = 288 K, sweep z to hit h*.

3.1: The column is hidden but the formula still holds. Write it on paper before touching the sliders.
3.2: Step 1: p*_atm = rho_Hg g h* (Pa). Step 2: pick p0, then z = H(T) ln(p0 / p*_atm).
3.3: Peek reveals the rearranged formula and the unit conversions. Then plug in the target h* shown on the tube.
